it does not explicitly state that Bangladesh submitted the declaration on that date."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0022-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"At an IAEA conference held November 6–10, 2023, a Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority presentation stated that the Government of Bangladesh contracted with the Russian government to set up two Rooppur nuclear power units and considered construction of an approximately 11,500 m3 interim disposal facility for very low-level radioactive waste at the plant site.","notes":["The excerpt says the government contracted with the Russian government; “agreement” is narrowed to the excerpt’s wording.","The excerpt says the paper considers construction of the facility; it does not establish a finalized proposal or operational status."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0022-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0022-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0022-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0022-E010","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"A 2017 assessment reported that the Bangladesh government's Rooppur project involved two VVER-1200 reactors, while Bangladesh, as a newcomer to nuclear power, needed national nuclear-safety infrastructure, an effective regulatory body, competent personnel, and safety culture. It noted limited nuclear-safety manpower and research resources, no safety laboratory at BAEC or the regulatory body, and the need for coordinated policy, education, research, and training.","notes":["The excerpt attributes the project decision to the Government of Bangladesh, not specifically to a Hasina government.","The excerpt calls for an effective regulatory body but does not specify that it must be independent."]}]}
